newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt desert development project to cost $810 mln.
newsitem.headline: Egypt desert development project to cost $810 mln.

text.p: The Egyptian government's ambitious plan to irrigate the Western Desert will initially cost 2.76 billion pounds ($810 million) spread over four years, the government newspaper al-Akhbar said on Sunday.

The bill includes two billion pounds over four years for a massive pumping station on the banks of the lake behind the Aswan High Dam and 760 million pounds over 30 months for a canal to take the water north from the Toshka depression, it said.

Government officials have said they can finance the project without adding to the government's budget deficit, which at about 1.1 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) is one of the prides of its economic reform programme.
But Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri has also said the government will not raise taxes at least until the financial year 1997/8 ends in June 1998.
Other elements being equal, the extra expenditure could increase the budget deficit by about 25 percent, according to extrapolations from central bank figures.

The idea of the project is to irrigate 500,000 acres (200,000 hectares) in the desert valley south of the oasis of Kharga. The government says this will relieve the population pressure on the Nile Valley, where more than 90 percent of the 60 million Egyptians live on four percent of Egypt's land area.
Work has already started on digging the canal and President Hosni Mubarak is expected to inaugurate the project this week in a grand ceremony at the site of the pumping station. ($=3.4 pounds)
